kernel: rikirinjani/dqf-label-safety-sourcing-cpu (v3 + v4 re-pick for glyburide, rosiglitazone, lovastatin)
status: PROPOSED ONLY - no drugs.json changes until user approval
approval_gate: Evidence file for user review (N6 pattern). Apply only after explicit APPROVED; statin pregnancy downgrade is a separate yes/no.
method: Kaggle CPU kernel fetches DailyMed v2 SPL (Rx, single-entity, best section coverage among up to 8-10 candidates) -> section + whole-document sentence sweep -> ordered rules in this script; every value carries its deciding quote

statin_pregnancy_downgrade.note: Current labels no longer list pregnancy as a contraindication (8.1: 'Discontinue ... when pregnancy is recognized'; FDA 2021 statin class labeling change). Proposed value normalizes to D, so these 5 drugs would LEAVE the pregnancy_x hard gate (still -6 safety penalty).

lovastatin_label_lag.note: Every lovastatin label on DailyMed (10 checked, 2026) is old-format and still lists 'Pregnancy and lactation' under CONTRAINDICATIONS -> X, inconsistent with the other 5 statins. Proposed per label as found.

stale_label.note: Only label available: AVANDIA 2010-01-19 (rosiglitazone); glyburide single-entity label chosen is Teva 2015 old-format (newer generics share the same text).

pre_pllr_category_letter.note: Label states a letter category (C / B); proposed verbatim as the letter.

not_in_dailymed.note: Not US-approved; no DailyMed SPL. Fields stay null; needs EMA SmPC sourcing round.

hepatic_label_silent.note: No hepatic impairment guidance found in label text; hepatic_safety stays null.

ace_inhibitor_hepatic_basis.note: hepatic 'caution' rests on the class idiosyncratic hepatic-failure warning (discontinue if jaundice), not on impairment dosing (ramipril also cites raised exposure).

new_hepatic_hard_gate.note: rosuvastatin/pravastatin: current labels list acute liver failure / decompensated cirrhosis (stored values were caution/safe). Label contraindication is specific (active liver disease / severe impairment / cirrhosis) but the current hepatic_contraindicated rule fires on ANY non-normal hepatic_function, including mild - see the open hepatic-rule policy item.
